labctl.notes: HOST-NATIVE since 2026-08-25: the museum's fork of Previous runs on the host as an unprivileged account under SDL's dummy video/audio drivers -- no captured Debian, no QEMU, no QMP, no X server, no window. Frames IFB1 shm, input mamectl/1, audio FIFO. `labctl exec` has no channel here: the NeXT's own exec is telnet to the guest on the retronet, driven by scripts/build-guests/nextstep-nstel.py with NSTEL_HOST=10.99.0.25 NSTEL_PORT=23 (log in as `me`, which su's for you; both are passwordless). Reset is a CRIU restore of the golden, ~3 s; see docs/guests/nextstep.md.

museum.blurb: The workstation Steve Jobs built after Apple threw him out, and the software that outlived the hardware: object-oriented Unix with a Display PostScript screen, whose NS-prefixed frameworks became Cocoa and are still what every Mac and iPhone app is written against. Tim Berners-Lee wrote the first web browser on one.
museum.notes: Live streamhost station, HOST-NATIVE since 2026-08-25. The museum's fork of the **Previous** emulator runs directly on the host as an unprivileged account under SDL's dummy video and audio drivers -- no captured Debian kiosk, no QEMU, no X server, no window -- as a colour **NeXTstation** (Motorola 68040 at 25 MHz, 32 MB, ROM Rev 2.5 v66) booting NeXTSTEP 3.3 for m68k off a SCSI disk image. It publishes its own three planes straight to the daemon: each changed frame into a shared IFB1 mapping with a real dirty rect, keyboard and absolute pointer over a mamectl/1 control socket, and 48 kHz PCM down a named pipe. The display is the NeXT MegaPixel's exact 1120x832, so nothing is ever resampled. This is deliberately NOT the Intel build of NeXTSTEP, which cannot survive a modern QEMU's SCSI/IDE timing -- see docs/guests/nextstep.md. The machine is a colour slab rather than the mono cube it used to emulate because colour costs nothing (measured: 148.5% of a core against 146.3%) and NeXTSTEP 3.3 boots the same unmodified disk on it with no in-guest change at all. Pointer is ABSOLUTE through the machine's own hardware: Previous emulates a SummaGraphics digitiser on the NeXT's serial port B and NeXTSTEP's own tablet driver is attached inside the checkpoint, so the coordinate a browser sends is the pixel the NeXT arrow lands on; the guest draws that arrow itself. The station is on the museum's retronet at 10.99.0.25 and browses the period corpus with OmniWeb 2.7b3. archetype mono-terminal; the ideal asset is a bespoke matte-black slab.

reset.fixture: NeXTstation Color (Motorola 68040, 25 MHz, 32 MB, ROM Rev 2.5 v66) running NeXTSTEP 3.3 for m68k in the museum's fork of Previous, HOST-NATIVE: the colour Workspace on its blue-grey #555577 root, the File Viewer open on the home directory, OmniWeb 2.7b3 in the Dock and its window showing the 8 May 1998 www.apple.com from the retronet corpus, fetched over the guest's own veth at 10.99.0.25. Baked 2026-08-25 as a CRIU checkpoint of the emulator process paired with the disk image reflinked inside the same freeze window; restore is ~3 s and the framebuffer comes back md5-identical, proven across two kill+restore cycles with a fresh corpus page fetched afterwards. Mouse PASS: the guest's SummaGraphics tablet driver is attached AND streaming inside the checkpoint, and 6 of 6 commanded absolute targets landed at 0 px on the colour machine, before and after a restore. Keyboard PASS: every one of the keymap's 80 rows was driven through the live control socket, and the scene itself is built by typing (type-select `omni`, Command-u, Command-q). See docs/guests/nextstep.md.

retronet.link: veth nextrn0 (host) <-> nextrn1 (netns nextstep-rn) on vmbr-rn

notes: Host-native: the museum's fork of Previous (github.com/Wnt/previous, branch kernel-hive) on the host, no kiosk guest
Previous MUST be built with -DENABLE_RENDERING_THREAD=1 or guest input is silently dropped
The emulator runs as an unprivileged account ON PURPOSE: SDL opens /dev/input/event* as root and criu cannot dump a character-device fd
Reset is a CRIU restore of the golden against its PAIRED disk reflink; a cold boot is the bounded fallback and comes up with a DEGRADED relative pointer
media (NeXT ROM + NeXTSTEP disk image + OmniWeb) is fetched at build time and never committed
